items.stem: What is a primary reason to prefer a database-per-service in microservices?

options.text: So each service owns its data and can evolve its schema independently
options.rationale: Correct: independent data ownership reduces coupling between services.

options.text: Because sharing one database is impossible
options.rationale: Sharing is possible but discouraged; it is not impossible.

options.text: Because it guarantees strong consistency across all services
options.rationale: Database-per-service typically embraces eventual consistency, not strong global consistency.

options.text: Because it removes the need for any API contracts
options.rationale: Services still need contracts to communicate.

items.explanation: Correct: independent data ownership reduces coupling between services.

items.stem: Which two patterns improve resilience when one service calls another over the network? (Select TWO)

options.text: Timeouts with bounded retries and backoff
options.rationale: Correct: timeouts and controlled retries prevent waiting forever and limit load.

options.text: A circuit breaker that stops calling a failing dependency
options.rationale: Correct: a circuit breaker prevents cascading failure.

options.text: Retrying immediately and indefinitely on every error
options.rationale: Unbounded immediate retries amplify load and can cause a storm.

options.text: Removing all error handling to simplify the code

items.explanation: Correct: timeouts and controlled retries prevent waiting forever and limit load.; Correct: a circuit breaker prevents cascading failure.

items.stem: A team splits a system into services but every request still needs all of them to be up together. What problem does this indicate?

options.text: A distributed monolith, where services are coupled and cannot deploy or fail independently
options.rationale: Correct: tight runtime coupling defeats the purpose of microservices.

options.text: A correctly decomposed set of microservices
options.rationale: Independent deploy and failure are missing, so it is not well decomposed.

options.text: A monolith with no network calls
options.rationale: There are services and network calls; it is distributed.
The symptom describes coupling, not a serverless model.

items.explanation: Correct: tight runtime coupling defeats the purpose of microservices.
